title: Riverton's new bus service
brief: Understand the cost, evidence and opening date of a fictional city's proposed bus service. Distinguish forecasts from observed results.
goals: What is the evidence for the improvement?
disclosure: Original fictional script, authored for Nonius. Both roles use synthetic speech. This is not a real interview or user study.

turns.speaker: Reporter
turns.text: What will the new bus service change for people in Riverton?

turns.speaker: Source
turns.text: We expect journeys to be twenty percent faster. That is the main benefit for passengers.

turns.speaker: Reporter
turns.text: Twenty percent faster compared with what, and is that a forecast or a measured result?

turns.speaker: Source
turns.text: It is a forecast compared with the March 2025 timetable. We have not measured the results yet.

turns.speaker: Source
turns.text: The approved budget is fifteen million pounds. Sorry, I mean fifty million pounds, including the new vehicles.

turns.speaker: Reporter
turns.text: When should passengers expect the new service to open?

turns.speaker: Source
turns.text: We are planning to open next spring. The exact date depends on the construction schedule.

turns.speaker: Reporter
turns.text: Which documents can readers use to check those figures?

turns.speaker: Source
turns.text: The transport committee will publish the business case after its next meeting. It will include the forecast assumptions and the full budget.
